blindQuestionRepair.originalQuery: After both reports flag, what is P(D)?

questions.feedback: Correctly conditions on the both-positive group, adds 900 D and 900 not-D, and distinguishes reversed conditioning and an unconditional joint denominator.

transfer.derivation: P(D and both flags)=900/16000=9/160. This uses all 16000 files; P(D | both flags)=900/1800 uses the 1800 both-positive files.

transfer.result: Matching separate counts do not establish matching file sets.
transfer.derivation: All three models have 1200 D flags per report and 3600 not-D flags per report, yet D overlaps are 900,1200,800 respectively. A counterexample already disproves an inference of exact copying.

questions.feedback: Correctly identifies the ++ conditional ratio 900/(900+900)=1/2 and explains each distractor's event or denominator.

transfer.derivation: At new prior 1/5 and unchanged within-class joint rates 9/16 and 1/16, class contributions are (1/5)(9/16)=9/80 and (4/5)(1/16)=4/80. Normalize 9/(9+4)=9/13. This is a new probability model; original finite population counts are not silently relabeled.

questions.feedback: Correctly states both class-conditioned product identities and distinguishes matching marginals from either class-conditioned or pooled independence.

transfer.result: P(F1+)=P(F2+)=3/10; P(F1+ and F2+)=9/80; pooled independence fails.
transfer.derivation: Each pooled flag set has 1200+3600=4800 files, while pooled ++ has 900+900=1800. Thus 4800/16000=3/10 and 1800/16000=9/80, which differs from (3/10)^2=9/100.
transfer.wordingFinding: Original transfer omitted tuple cell order. The corrected immutable source adds (++,+-,-+,--) order, first-sign report1 and +/− meanings without changing counts or calculation. It resolves the standalone notation finding; exact inverse returns the original lesson.

questions.answerContent: The reports are independent within D and within not-D.

questions.feedback: Correctly uses +- counts 300 and 2700 and the appropriate second-negative likelihood ratio 1/3 inside the first-positive group.

transfer.derivation: The -- cell has 100 D and 8100 not-D files. P(D | --)=100/(100+8100)=1/82, and D:not-D odds are 100:8100=1:81.

questions.feedback: Correctly retains F1+ in both second-positive likelihood conditions, gives p*a/[p*a+(1-p)*b], and requires a positive denominator.

transfer.derivation: Within first-positive D, denominators are 900+300=1200,1200+0=1200,800+400=1200. Numerators are 900,1200,800. Within first-positive not-D denominators are 900+2700=3600,3600+0=3600,3600+0=3600; numerators are 900,3600,3600.

questions.answerContent: P(F2+ | F1+, D) and P(F2+ | F1+, not-D)

questions.feedback: Correctly identifies equal first-positive and both-positive events, unchanged posterior 1/4, and conditional likelihood ratio 1.

transfer.derivation: A third exact copy creates no smaller conditioning set: the all-three-positive event equals the first-positive event, with 1200 D and 3600 not-D. Therefore 1200/4800=1/4. Matching marginal rates alone would not establish this event equality.

questions.feedback: Correctly computes 800/4400=2/11 while retaining the unchanged individual class rates and warning against importing the independent product.

transfer.derivation: Dependent +- contains 400 D and 0 not-D. Its denominator 400 is positive, so 400/(400+0)=1. P(+-)=400/16000=1/40. The conclusion is exact for this supplied table and establishes no guarantee in a real report system.

questions.feedback: Correctly uses conditional rates (800/1200)/(3600/3600)=2/3, posterior odds 2:9 and probability 2/11. It explains why a standalone positive can lower an already-conditioned posterior.

transfer.derivation: At new first-positive posterior 2/5 with conditional rates a=2/3,b=1, D contribution is 4/15 and not-D contribution 9/15. Their normalized D share is 4/13. Equivalently odds 2:3 multiply by 2/3 to become 4:9.

questions.feedback: Correctly identifies single-report posterior 1/4 while leaving both-positive posterior unidentified by the marginal summaries; the three exact tables are explicit countermodels.

transfer.result: Copied both-positive posterior 1/4; dependent 2/11, with the same prior and both reports' class marginals.
transfer.derivation: Copied D++1200 versus dependent D++800 changes the overlap. Both models have D marginal flags 1200 for each report: dependent adds 400 in each disagreement cell and has D--0, while copied has both disagreement cells0 and D--400. Their not-D rows are identical, class totals1600/14400 and prior1/10 remain fixed.

questions.feedback: Correctly separates an undefined 0/0 conditional from probability0 or1, and identifies disagreement as outside the exact-copy model's support.

transfer.result: A genuine disagreement contradicts the stated exact-copy finite population model, without supplying a replacement posterior.
transfer.derivation: Both disagreement cells are empty in both classes. An actual disagreement therefore cannot be a sampled outcome of that exact population. The mismatch does not identify its cause, a replacement joint model, or the true rework probability; no numerical posterior follows from 0/0.

questions.answerContent: Undefined: the conditioning event has probability zero
